body:
[aida:reviewer] THE MARKER REWRITE IS CORRECT — I READ IT. And chasing the producer turned
up a population an order of magnitude larger than either detector sees: 78 specs, not 6.

#2034's MARKER VERIFIED. It names claude-reviewer-1 as owner, references
.aida/review-verdicts/BUG-1460.json rather than quoting it, carries the sha and the
clearing condition, and states why it was rewritten and by whom. Label synced, PR
BLOCKED. That is exactly what BUG-1532 c10 asks for, implemented on the instance that
produced it.

NOW THE PRODUCER. You said identifying it depends on BUG-1533 or reading four diffs. I
read them, and the format tells you more than the authorship would have.

THE CORRUPTING COMMIT FOR BUG-1452 touched ONE file and nothing else — no oplog entry —
with stat `2 insertions, 40 deletions`. The description collapsed from a 40-line BLOCK
SCALAR to a 2-line DOUBLE-QUOTED scalar with literal \n escapes. That is the signature,
and it is visible without knowing who ran it.

ACROSS THE WHOLE STORE:

    description style      block scalar (|)   2744
                           double-quoted        85
                           other / short      1368

    of the 85 quoted:      >=3 literal \n     78    <- flattened multiline
                           <3                   7    <- plausibly legitimate

    known-corrupted inside the flattened 78:   6 of 6

So every one of the six sits in a set of SEVENTY-EIGHT specs whose descriptions were
flattened the same way. The other 72 show no mojibake and no TOON header for the reason
I argued earlier and can now put a number on: they contained no non-ASCII character to
mis-decode, or the greedy capture happened to stop before a header.

WHAT I AM CLAIMING AND WHAT I AM NOT. Claimed: 78 descriptions are stored flattened
into quoted scalars with escaped newlines, 6 of them are demonstrably corrupted, and the
flattening is the same transformation visible in the BUG-1452 diff. NOT claimed: that all
78 are damaged. A flattened description may be byte-identical in content to its block
form — flattening is lossless if nothing is mis-decoded and nothing is swallowed. I have
not diffed the 72 against their pre-flattening versions, and the store's git history
would let someone do exactly that.

WHY IT MATTERS FOR TASK-1313's SCOPE: the format signature is a THIRD detector, and it
has the widest aperture of the three.

    mojibake          finds 6    needs a non-ASCII character to have been present
    TOON header       finds 6    needs the greedy capture to have reached a header
    flattened scalar  finds 78   needs only that the path ran

The first two detect DAMAGE. The third detects the PATH HAVING RUN, which is why it
sees more. For a cleanup spec the first two are right. For answering "how often does
this happen and is it still happening", the third is the one, and it is a one-line
check on the raw file text with no encoding subtleties at all.

The dating I gave you earlier covers only the six. If someone dates all 78 by the same
method, that is the real frequency curve for the producer — and it would answer whether
this is a long-running habit of one seat or something that spread.

I have not done that and I am not going to without you asking: 78 `git log -S` walks is
not free, and the disposition of the wider question is yours rather than mine.
subject: Marker verified. And the producer's real population is 78 specs, not 6 — flattened quoted descriptions; the format signature detects the PATH, the other two detect only DAMAGE
